title: Slow-cooker shredded beef tacos
subtitle: Pull-apart spiced beef for corn tacos
excerpt: Beef chuck cooked with cumin, chilli, and garlic until it shreds effortlessly. Pile into corn tortillas with your choice of toppings for a very good taco night.
sourceNotes: Shredded beef tacos using slow-cooked beef chuck are a Tex-Mex and Mexican-American home-cooking staple. The cut and method draw on the tradition of barbacoa, where tough cuts are cooked low and slow until very tender.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shredded beef in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat in a pan.
recipe.batchNotes: Excellent batch recipe. The shredded beef keeps for 5 days in the fridge and suits tacos, burritos, and rice bowls.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook a day ahead and refrigerate. The spiced beef is even better the next day as the flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Beef chuck is the right cut for this recipe. It is well marbled with fat and connective tissue that breaks down over a long cook and keeps the meat moist and flavourful as it shreds. Lean cuts such as topside will dry out and produce a stringy, tough result.
Cook the beef for a full 8 hours on LOW. At 6 hours it may be tender enough to shred, but at 8 hours it will shred far more easily and the flavour will be deeper.
Serve in warm corn tortillas with soured cream, sliced jalapeños, and fresh coriander. Lime juice over everything at the end makes a big difference.

items.prepNote: in one or two large pieces

content.text: Add {{onion}} sliced onion and {{garlic}} of crushed garlic to the slow cooker. Place {{beef-chuck}} of beef chuck on top. Mix all the dry spices together and rub over the beef. Pour over {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes and {{stock-beef}} of beef stock. Season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 7 to 8 hours. The beef should pull apart very easily with two forks. Lift it out and shred it on a board. Return the shredded beef to the pot and stir it through the cooking juices. Squeeze in {{lime}} lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

rows.symptom: The beef is not shredding after 8 hours
rows.cause: Very large pieces of chuck can take longer to break down, especially if they are thick.
rows.fix: Cook on HIGH for a further hour. The muscle fibres will eventually give way. Check again after 30 minutes on HIGH.

rows.cause: The chuck released a lot of fat and liquid during the long cook.
rows.fix: Lift the shredded beef out with a slotted spoon and serve it slightly dry. Pour any excess fat off the cooking liquid, then reduce it in a pan for 10 minutes and spoon it back over the beef.

rows.symptom: The flavour is bland despite the spices
rows.cause: The spices diluted over a long cook in a large volume of liquid.
rows.fix: Squeeze in extra lime juice. Add a pinch of smoked paprika and cumin to the shredded meat and stir well before serving.

rows.symptom: The beef is dry and stringy
rows.cause: A leaner cut was used, or the beef was cooked too long without enough liquid.
rows.fix: Stir the shredded meat through all the cooking juices. Next time ensure the liquid comes at least a third of the way up the beef before cooking.

content.text: Shredded beef tacos draw on the barbacoa tradition of Mexican cooking, where tough cuts are cooked very low and very slow in a sealed environment. The slow cooker replicates the sealed-pot method that gives barbacoa its characteristic texture. The dish crossed into British homes through Tex-Mex cooking and has become a firm fixture of taco nights.
